correctness.rationale: Universal Banach extension lower bound follows by extending the canonical map into the finite Lipschitz-free space F(X); images of hubs give affine coefficients and a constant-preserving linear scalar extension of the same norm. Conversely, any scalar extension operator extends every Banach-valued map with the same factor. Averaging over S_m×S_m×C2 reduces all signed-coefficient linear candidates to α. For each leaf-supported zero-total-mass measure, exact tree transportation norm is Σ|mass at leaves|+t|mass of A|; applying it to central edge and each pendant edge yields norm max{1,F(α),((t+2)/t)|2α−1|} with F=|α/m−1|+(m−1)|α|/m+(1+t)|1−α|. Piecewise slopes show no α outside [1/2,1] is better. On this interval F decreases linearly and central term increases linearly; their crossing α*=(t+1)(t+2)/(t²+(2+2/m)t+4) is feasible up to t=2m/(m−2) when m>2; otherwise optimum α=1 and value 2−2/m. At m=2 intersection remains feasible for all t, and its value tends to one as t→∞. Fifteen independent exact-rational parameter checks (not a general proof) reproduced both branches.
